sections.overview: This Mexican highland rattlesnake is also called the Querétaro dusky rattlesnake; it is a close relative of C. triseriatus, with which it was historically grouped.
sections.identification: It is robust and gray-brown, with dark dorsal blotches, paired dark nape marks and pale-edged lateral stripes.
sections.habitat: Mexican natural-history records place it in temperate pine–oak woodland, mesquite scrub and grassland on the central plateau and eastern highlands.
sections.diet: Field observations recorded mammals, lizards and other snakes as prey, suggesting a varied diet that can include other snakes.
sections.behavior: The CONABIO report describes it as active by day and at twilight.
sections.reproduction: The sources consulted here do not provide a robust species-specific account of breeding timing or litter size.
sections.ecology: By consuming rodents and other vertebrates, it is a predator of highland grassland and woodland food webs.
sections.conservation: Mexico’s NOM-059 lists it under special protection (Pr); this national legal category is distinct from a global IUCN assessment.
